modules.title: All Types of Health Institutions — Minimum Requirements
modules.sourceHeading: MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS- FOR ALL TYPES OF HEALTH INSTITUTIONS
modules.notes: Enforcement/governance context, verbatim-faithful: 'Failure to display HPA Certificate will result in a fine' (p16). PLEASE NOTE passage (pp18-19): facilities with the following shortfalls shall be registered while they attend to the shortfalls within a week as the items are not critical and will not affect the functioning of the facilities — bin liners; liquid soap and appropriate non-usable hand drying facilities; proof of medical waste disposal; screens and footstools (pp18-19). Where facilities are considered grossly inadequate (failing to meet the minimum requirements), the Health Institution shall be closed (p19). For Routine Inspections, practitioners are usually given a month in which to attend to the noted shortfalls (p19). The PLEASE NOTE obligation 'Practitioners shall not to open their premises until they have been registered with the Health Professions Authority' (p18) is an inspectable obligation and is captured as item ALL-052.

modules.title: Conventional Radiology — Minimum Requirements
modules.notes: Section opens with a cross-reference: 'Other requirements are as stated under "Minimum requirements for all types of Health Institutions"' (page 31) — see the common all-institutions module; not repeated as items here.

measurement.expected: at least 20 square meters floor area and more than 3 m height as stated
measurement.dimension: radiography room floor area and ceiling height

items.requirement: Conventional radiography room size shall be at least 20 square meters in floor area and more than 3m in height.

measurement.expected: not less than 1.2 m and 2 m height as stated; door shielded

items.requirement: Room entrance shall not be less than 1.2m and 2 meters height, with shielded door.

items.quantity: at least one designated patient gowning area

measurement.expected: at least 1.5 m x 1.2 m as stated

items.requirement: At least one designated patient gowning area for patient changing with safe storage for valuables and clothing shall be provided. At least this area shall be 1.5 meters x 1.2 meters with immediate access to the conventional radiography room.
Wall finish shall be general paint.
Floor finish: vinyl composition tile.
Shielded viewing window from the Control Area to the conventional radiography room.

measurement.dimension: X-ray room surface and shielding thickness

items.requirement: Minimum X-ray room surfaces and shielding thicknesses in compliance with RPAZ requirement.
Fluorescent lights will provide higher illumination level up to 540 Candela during patient transfer on and from the table, equipment setting, room cleaning, and equipment maintenance.

measurement.expected: at least 2 meters square as stated

items.requirement: If film systems are used, a darkroom shall be provided for processing films (at least 2 meters square) with water basin, table, benches, film holder and safe light.
items.applicability: where film systems are used

items.requirement: When daylight processing is used, the darkroom shall be permitted to be minimal for emergency and special uses.
items.alternatives: a minimal darkroom for emergency and special uses is permitted when daylight processing is used
items.applicability: when daylight processing is used

items.requirement: Film processing shall be located near the procedure rooms and to the quality control area.
If contrast media are used, this area shall include provision of sink, counter, and storage area for medication and crash cart.
items.applicability: if contrast media are used

items.requirement: Provision for central oxygen or oxygen cylinder.
Appropriate emergency equipment and medications must be immediately available to treat adverse reactions associated with administered medication.
One preparation room, if conveniently located, shall be permitted to serve any number of rooms.
items.alternatives: a single conveniently located preparation room is permitted to serve any number of rooms

items.requirement: Where pre-prepared media are used, this area shall be permitted to be omitted, but storage shall be provided for the media.
items.alternatives: the preparation area may be omitted where pre-prepared media are used, provided storage is provided for the media
items.applicability: where pre-prepared media are used

items.requirement: Convenient clerical offices/spaces as per the facility demand.

items.conditional: not required where the room is used only for routine screening such as chest X-rays where the patient is not physically handled by the staff
items.requirement: Hand-washing stations shall be provided within each procedure room unless the room is used only for routine screening such as chest X-rays where the patient is not physically handled by the staff.
Radiology equipment and supplies include but not limited to the listed items.
X-ray machine with X-ray table with wall block.
Lead aprons.
Gonad shields.
Immobilizers.
Cassette and grids.
Emergency trolley.
Working table with bench.
X-ray viewer.
Foot step to help patients to step in to X-ray table.
Computed Radiography (CR).
Lead apron hanger.
Computer work station.
Green/Red warning light sign indicating when the X-ray beam is OFF/ON.
X-ray caution sign on the tube housing.
Designated supply storage and housekeeping area.

modules.title: Laboratory — Minimum Requirements
modules.notes: Section opens with a cross-reference (page 43): 'Other requirements are as stated under "Minimum requirements for all types of Health Institutions"' — the common all-institutions module applies in addition to these items.

measurement.expected: at least 15 m2 per room as stated

items.requirement: Main laboratory minimum space – 15m2 per room. Laboratory design and equipment arrangement should be compatible
Floors — non-absorbent, non-slippery and easily washable
Adequate ventilation and lighting provided by both natural and artificial means
Provision to prevent unauthorized access to the laboratory
Patient reception and bleeding room – separate from other room. To cater for disabled people
Work benches — non-absorbent and easily washable
Separate incompatible activities i.e. office and laboratory work
Storage facilities
Examination and processing of highly infectious material to be carried out in appropriate containment level laboratories
items.applicability: laboratories examining or processing highly infectious material

items.requirement: Media preparation room (microbiology) — separate from rest of laboratory
items.applicability: microbiology laboratories

items.requirement: Sharps boxes at each working area
Separate patients and staff toilets
Staff kitchen/tea room with sink – for meals and teas
Controlled lighting, temperature an ventilation – as per relevant act
Location of laboratory shall comply with local authority laws
Constant supply of clean water, power supply and backup
Use of environmentally friendly reagents and methods
Recruitment of qualified and competent staff responsible for safety
Employ pest control measures methods to prevent vermin, insects and other pests
Provide the following items
Safety Manual/Handbook
Guideline Operating Procedures
Work instructions
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) i.e. gloves, respirators, safety shoes, laboratory coats
Disinfectants at appropriate concentrations for various uses
Biological Safety cabinets
Guidelines procedures for decontamination (where applicable)
Maintained Eye-Wash facilities
Serviced fire extinguisher
Facilities for containment and disposal of waste
Procedure for management of accidents i.e. spill kit
Maintained first aid kit equipment and items

Specimen collection and handling, transportation, reception and referral to other laboratories in accordance with adequate safety measures (outlined in safety manual, local and international regulations)
Well documented procedure for decontamination of equipment and laboratory surfaces
Sufficient safety notices and labelling of laboratory environment
Well documented procedure for dealing with exposure of staff to hazardous material — Vaccination; Immunization protocol; Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)
Policies and procedures for relevant vaccination and medical examinations for staff. (Adequate consent and counselling must be provided)
Procedure for appropriate use and disposal of obsolete equipment
Procedure for action in the event of fire (fire drill/control)
Procedure for action in event of major spillage of dangerous chemicals or clinical materials
Clean, uncluttered and well maintained work areas (have good housekeeping procedures)
Gases, acids and alcohols used in laboratory or testing site must be kept in safety containment areas in accordance with existing laws and regulations
Procedure for disposal of health care waste
Workable internal quality control systems — able to verify that best intended quality is achieved
Participation in external quality assurance programmes for each analyte and keep records

modules.title: Theatre — Minimum Requirements
modules.notes: Section opens with a cross-reference (page 53): 'Other requirements are as stated under "Minimum requirements for all types of Health Institutions"' — the common all-institutions module applies in addition to these items. The section includes a 'POLICY ON RECOVERY ROOM STAFF' passage (pages 57-59); its concrete staffing/process obligations are captured as items, while the following policy narration is context only: staff qualifications, staffing levels, standardised minimum equipment, clinical techniques and clinical competence to decide next therapeutic manoeuvres are 'critically important for successful outcomes' (page 57); 'There is no absolute numbers of staffing levels, but state of occupancy and condition of patients dictate how best to deal with staffing levels. This should be determined at the point of providing anaesthetic service' (page 57); as a patient emerges from unconsciousness and begins to cooperate, 'one nurse could look after two patients on adjacent stations' (page 57); a patient arriving in the recovery room has a variable level of consciousness, from fully conscious (local or regional anaesthesia) to comatose (page 58); some patients may be restless or agitated post-operatively (pain, fear, full bladder, child) and may require more than one staff member until settled — self-injury is a risk (page 58); 'It is difficult to give guidance on the exact numbers of staff required' — staffing levels depend on case mix, numbers of patients and number of operating lists per session (page 59); staffing the recovery room is described as 'an ongoing intractable problem' — all staffing statements are minimal staff-to-patient ratios dependent on the clinical status of the patient, it 'remains doubtful that a magic formula can be developed', and safe staffing 'is still dependent on the expertise of the Charge Nurse who can adjust staffing if necessary on a day to day basis' (page 59).

Anaesthetic and post anaesthetic care is administered in specifically designated, equipped, and staffed registered hospitals/institutions by appropriately qualified and registered personnel or trainees under supervision of registered clinicians

The Anaesthetist leads a team of medical and nursing practitioners charged with the responsibility of ensuring complete recovery from the now undesired effects of anaesthetic drugs; pain control and stabilisation of vital functions is also an important consideration for this team especially in the first 24 hours
The recovery room charge Nurse should be able to vary staff levels very quickly and almost instantly, and call out for help if needed in a matter of an instant

items.conditional: applies when patient condition deteriorates suddenly and unexpectedly
items.requirement: Should patient condition deteriorate suddenly and unexpectedly, the Nurse immediately calls the Doctor and resuscitation team for help, which should be accorded in a matter of seconds; one patient may be attended to by a team of medical professionals as assessed appropriate in a rapidly changing situation (e.g. cardio pulmonary resuscitation)
In transporting a postoperative patient to the recovery room, the anaesthetist, the scrub nurse and a porter shall transport a stable patient lying in a hospital bed, appropriately monitored
The recovery room should receive the patient with a natural airway

Upon arrival, the anaesthetist attaches minimum monitors and fully evaluates the patient: pulse oximetry, electrocardiograph, pulse, automated interval blood pressure monitor and temperature, amongst others
items.reviewReason: Manual wording is garbled: 'These are pulse oximetry, conscious electrocardiograph pulse, automated interval blood pressure monitor and temperature, amongst others' (page 58) — the exact intended monitor list ('conscious electrocardiograph pulse') is unclear.

items.requirement: The anaesthetist physically hands over explained, written-down post-operative instructions for the care of the patient to the Nurse taking care of the patient in the recovery room, and ensures that there is complete understanding of the instructions; the Nurse examines the patient
Upon the Nurse accepting responsibility for the patient, the vital functions observations are documented
An accurate timed observation of respirations, pulse, blood pressure, pulse oximetry, amongst others, is documented

Reception of patient (patient may be unconscious or emergent from that state): staff ratio 1:2 (one patient / two nurses) to undertake handover, prioritise immediate care and set up monitoring; the skills of the first nurse must be appropriate for the acuity of the case; the helper may be a novice nurse or member of the perioperative team

Stabilisation period (self ventilating with no airway adjuncts or needing respiratory assistance): staff ratio 2:1 (two patients / one nurse); skills of nurse must be appropriate to acuity of cases; if the patient's condition deteriorates staff must be reallocated promptly

Fit for discharge (has met all local discharge criteria — is stable and comfortable): staff ratio 3:1 (three patients / one nurse); the nurse looking after three patients must be experienced and may be assisted by a novice or member of the perioperative team

items.quantity: no fewer than two staff, of whom at least one must be a registered practitioner
items.requirement: No fewer than two staff (of whom at least one must be a registered practitioner) should be present when there is a patient in the recovery room who does not fulfil the criteria for discharge to the ward
Until patients can maintain their airway, breathing and circulation they must be cared for on a one-to-one basis

items.quantity: at least two appropriately trained staff
items.requirement: At least two appropriately trained staff should be present in the recovery room while there is a patient who does not fulfil the criteria for discharge to the ward

items.requirement: Auditing variables that affect staff-patient ratios is recommended (delayed discharge being one important factor)
